name: Counter
description: A number whose digits roll like an odometer to reach the new value; digits and separators come from `Intl` itself, changes land with a spring and a stepped cascade, and fast-spinning digits pick up motion blur along the way.
interactionNotes: The component takes no input; you change the value from outside and the digits roll. The live demo has four scenes: a countdown that rolls over every second, a stats dashboard that moves live numbers up and down, a pricing scene that cycles through a monthly/annual segment and seat buttons, and a base scene where the minus/plus/random buttons shift the value. Each sample's entrance also has a welcome roll that plays as soon as it is seen.

props.name: value
props.description: The number shown; every change rolls the digits.

props.name: locale
props.description: Locale for separators, symbols, and digits; it defaults to Persian and takes its digits from it — pass another locale and the same component rolls with that script's digits.

props.name: format
props.description: Formatting options: currency, percent, unit, or compact notation.

props.name: decimals
props.description: Fixed number of decimal places; omit it to keep the format's default.

props.name: minDigits
props.description: Minimum digits in the integer part — leading zeros of the number.

props.name: prefix
props.description: Content before the number.

props.name: suffix
props.description: Content after the number.

props.name: direction
props.description: Roll direction; 'auto' goes up as the value grows and down as it shrinks.

props.name: duration
props.description: Approximately the length of one roll, in seconds.

props.name: bounce
props.description: How far the digits overshoot before settling, from 0 to 0.9.

props.name: stagger
props.description: Delay between neighboring digits, in seconds — the wave of change comes from this, and it falls from the right of the number.

props.name: motionBlur
props.description: Blur of fast-spinning digits along their path; it only activates during a fast roll.

props.name: intro
props.description: A full welcome roll as soon as half of the frame is visible — once per sample.

props.name: fade
props.description: How far (in em) a digit rolls outside the text before fading; zero means clipping at the edge.

props.name: fontSize
props.description: Font size in px, or any CSS value such as "inherit".

props.name: fontWeight
props.description: Font weight of the number.

props.name: textColor
props.description: Color of the number; it defaults to the surrounding ink.

props.name: gap
props.description: Spacing between digits and symbols, px.

props.name: padding
props.description: Extra height per digit, px — it also opens up the roll space.

props.name: tabular
props.description: Equal widths for the digits; off means the width shifts smoothly between digits.

props.name: digitStyle
props.description: Style of each digit — for example tiling it with a background and rounding.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra class for the root.

props.name: style
props.description: Inline style of the root.

tips: Persian digits need no manual conversion: they come from `Intl.NumberFormat` with the locale. Pass another locale (Arabic, English…) and the same component rolls with that script's digits.
For a countdown, raise `padding` a little so the digits can breathe inside their tile and set `fade: 0` so the edge is clipped — the site demo uses exactly this combination.
`stagger` sets the character of the display: zero means all digits roll at once; above 0.1 a stepped wave falls from the right of the number.
On a weak phone, turn off `motionBlur` — the SVG filter only activates during a fast roll, but turning it off costs nothing.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the rolls settle instantly and the new value is shown directly; the entrance animation does not play at all.
This component does not mirror for right-to-left, and that is intentional: a number is a left-to-right run. Put the unit and label outside it so they land in the right place in a Persian layout.
Keep `tabular` on for tabular numeric columns; for a large single-number display turn it off so the width follows the digits smoothly.
